speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for your response. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific triggers for your chronic cough, such as exposure to dust, chemicals, or cold air? Also, have you ever smoked or been exposed to significant secondhand smoke?

REQUEST TEST: Spirometry
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Spirometry: FVC: Reduced, FEV1: Reduced, FEV1/FVC_Ratio: Normal; Chest_X-ray: Irregular opacities in the right middle lobe and diffuse airway thickening.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis. The mention of Pyelonephritis by the previous doctor is incorrect as it is a kidney infection and does not match your respiratory symptoms of productive cough and recurrent bronchitis. Spirometry and Chest X-Ray results will be reviewed to confirm lung function and rule out other causes like COPD or bronchiectasis.
